nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) with TA775 for SGLT2 inhibitors

medications.purpose: Renal protection and blood pressure control (already prescribed)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first_line ACE inhibitor for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension

medications.purpose: Glycaemic control for type 2 diabetes (already prescribed)
medications.nice_justification: Standard diabetes management; not a CKD‑specific recommendation

medications.purpose: Slow CKD progression and reduce proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 SGLT2 inhibitor indicated for CKD eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m² (TA775)
NG203 statin recommended for all CKD patients as a CVD risk‑equivalent

medications.purpose: Achieve BP target <130/80 mmHg (add-on to ACE‑I)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 add second antihypertensive agent if BP uncontrolled on ACE‑I alone

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive glucose‑lowering effect increasing risk of hypoglycaemia
interactions_checked.action: Reduce insulin dose by 10‑20 % and advise glucose monitoring

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential rise in serum potassium and modest eGFR decline
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K⁺ and creatinine 1‑2 weeks after start; hold or adjust if K⁺ >5.5 mmol/L or creatinine rises >30 %

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined antihypertensive effect may cause hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Start amlodipine at low dose, monitor BP and symptoms; adjust if symptomatic hypotension

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium not available – will obtain before adding amlodipine/chlorthalidone.
Baseline liver function tests not available – required before starting atorvastatin.
Albumin‑creatinine ratio (ACR) not recorded – assumed proteinuric based on urine dipstick protein 281 mg/dL.
QRISK score not calculated – CKD stage 3b qualifies patient as CVD risk‑equivalent per NG203.
Allergy status unknown – will confirm no statin or ACE‑I hypersensitivity before prescribing.
Alcohol intake moderate; patient has trace urine ketones – counsel on avoiding excess alcohol and monitor for euglycaemic ketoacidosis after starting dapagliflozin.
treatment_summary: Continue lisinopril and insulin. Add dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for renal protection, atorvastatin 20 mg daily for cardiovascular risk reduction, and amlodipine 5 mg daily to achieve BP <130/80 mmHg. Monitor electrolytes, renal function, liver enzymes, glucose, and ketones per NICE NG203. Provide lifestyle advice (low‑salt diet, smoking cessation, limit alcohol, exercise).
